chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic:
'And the witnesses should not refuse when they are summoned' [2:282].
So he said: 'It is not befitting for anyone who, when summoned to testify regarding what he has witnessed, to say: I shall not testify for you.'

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةُ: testimony/witnessing — the act of bearing legal witness before a judge or authority
key_terms.الشُّهَدَاءُ: witnesses — those who have personally observed an event and are legally capable of bearing testimony
key_terms.يَنْبَغِي: it is befitting/appropriate — indicates a strong moral or legal propriety, here in the negative: it is not proper

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the obligation of witnesses to testify when summoned?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the Quranic verse 2:282 which commands witnesses not to refuse when summoned to give testimony. The Imam clarifies that this obligation applies specifically to one who has already witnessed an event: such a person must not decline the call to testify. This ruling addresses the social and legal responsibility of witnesses in Islamic jurisprudence, protecting the rights of litigants who rely on eyewitness testimony for justice.
